description: We are SpacePaseA, a team passionate about space exploration, science, and innovative technologies. Our project focuses on identifying Earth locations that can serve as analogs for future Moon and Mars habitats using NASA data. We want to create an interactive solution that helps understand planetary environments and supports future human exploration. We are looking for teammates interested in coding, data analysis, AI, design, and space science.
summary:
SpacePace is a framework designed to identify the most suitable Earth analog locations for specific Moon and Mars mission objectives. Current analog site selection is often based on individual choices, without a standardized method for matching environments with mission requirements.

Our project introduces a weighted evaluation approach that compares Earth analog locations using criteria such as temperature extremes, dust conditions, terrain, geological similarity, and isolation. We demonstrate how different environments support different exploration tasks: Ustyurt Plateau for thermal endurance testing, Aralkum Desert for dust and optical system testing, and Murghab region for cold-weather robotics.

SpacePace aims to make analog selection more objective, transparent, and data-driven, supporting future planetary exploration planning.
details:
SpacePaseA addresses a key challenge in Moon and Mars exploration: selecting the right Earth analog environment for specific mission objectives.

Instead of searching for one location that is generally “Mars-like”, our framework identifies which environment is most suitable for a specific task, such as thermal testing, dust analysis, rover navigation, or geological research.

The project uses a mathematical weighted scoring method:

Weighted Score = Σ (criterion importance × site rating)

This approach combines environmental analysis and decision-making methods to compare locations using criteria such as temperature extremes, dust conditions, terrain, geological similarity, and isolation.

The framework demonstrates how:

• Ustyurt Plateau can support thermal endurance testing,

•Aralkum Desert can support dust and optical system testing,

• Murghab region can support cold-weather robotics research.

By combining scientific criteria, mathematical evaluation, and mission requirements, SpacePace provides a more objective approach to selecting Earth analog sites for future Moon and Mars missions.
